placements.why: This envelope's content is a calibration report: an instrument's tuning verified against a dated reference standard. Nothing in the (empty) existing strata covers organizational categories yet, and calibration/verification work is a recurring organizational-proof activity distinct from Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Architecture/Organization/Proof/Templates — minting it standalone gives future calibration envelopes a home.
placements.title: instrument calibration and verification as an organizational category
placements.frame: what instrument, standard, and verification act ground a claim that a calibration holds?

placements.title: calibration validity is anchored to reference-standard verification, not asserted alone
placements.frame: what reference standard was used to verify this instrument's calibration, and across what range does the verification claim to hold?
placements.why: src-1 and src-3 both ground the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration in verification against the June reference plates, holding across the full observing band — the same directional claim in narrative and summary-field form (matching the position CalibrationVerifiedAgainstReferencePlates). src-2 names the instrument this verification is performed on, anchoring the same record. This is a subject future calibration envelopes will keep feeding (more instruments, more reference checks), not a one-off fact, so it passes the narrative grain test rather than being folded as a bare data point.
